chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said regarding the traveler who enters his family during the month of Ramadan and had eaten before his entry: He should refrain from eating for the remainder of his day, and upon him is the making up (of the fast).

And He (peace be upon him) said regarding the traveler who enters his family while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) before midday, and had not eaten: Upon him is that he completes his fast, and there is no making up for it upon him, meaning when his impurity was from a wet dream.

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday (when the sun begins to decline)
key_terms.جُنُب: In a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan having eaten or being in a state of impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between breaking the fast due to consumption versus remaining valid despite ritual impurity, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the continuity of the day's fast. It establishes that a traveler who arrives in a state of janabah (major impurity) before midday (zawal) without having eaten retains the validity of his fast for that day, requiring no makeup (qada), provided the impurity was not self-induced through deliberate eating or drinking. This ruling underscores the Shia view that the state of impurity itself does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing it from the act of breaking the fast through consumption.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus who said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the traveler who comes over to his family during a Month of Ramazan and he had eaten before his coming over, said: ‘He should refrain from eating for the remainder of his day, and upon him would be its making up’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the traveler who comes over to his family and he is with sexual impurity before the midday and did not happen to have eaten, so upon him is that he completes his Fast and there is no making up for it upon him, meaning when he was with sexual impurity from the bed-wetting’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Ubayd from Yunus who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who arrives from a journey in his family in the month of Ramadan and has already used food before his arrival, he (the Imam) said, that he must abstain from eating for the rest of the day and he is required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fasting).’

About a traveler who arrives in his family before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) and has not used any food but has experienced a wet dream, he is required to complete that fast. He is not required to carry out Qada’ (compensatory fast) for it, that is, if his experience is because of wet dream.’”
